questionText: Which of the following is/are part of an Instruction Set Architecture of a processor?
options: The size of the cache memory
The clock frequency of the processor
The number of cache memory levels
explanation:
Step-by-step Explanation:

• Instruction Set Architecture (ISA): The ISA defines the abstract model of a computer that is visible to the programmer or compiler. It includes the instruction set, addressing modes, data types, and programmer-visible architectural state such as the total number of registers.

• Microarchitectural Features:
- Cache size and number of levels (Options A & C) are microarchitectural implementation details and are transparent to the ISA.
- Clock frequency (Option B) is a hardware implementation parameter.

Hence, only Option (D) is a part of the Instruction Set Architecture.
